What to do: Split the override switch into two things: 'apply this value' and 'lock this value'
Why it matters: Right now override means opposite things in two places, so there is NO way to say 'everyone gets this and nobody may change it' - the most common thing an admin wants
Notes: Dialpad separates a template (seeds values) from a User Settings Policy (locks them). Copy that. Affects every setting on the company page

What to do: Check permissions on the server, not just in the browser
Why it matters: Today the permission tree only hides buttons. Any signed-in user can send any request - including making themselves an admin
Notes: Biggest security item on the list. Nothing else on this sheet matters if this stays open

What to do: Actually route the emergency address to the carrier
Why it matters: We collect and validate it properly but it is never attached to an emergency call. This is the only item with legal and safety weight
Notes: Dialpad refuses to let a company go live without this. Also add: who the address applies to, and notification contacts

What to do: Enforce the fraud controls we already store
Why it matters: External transfer, transferring your own outbound call, and international dialling are all stored and none are enforced. Toll fraud on a new account can be company-ending
Notes: Dialpad ships all three OFF by default for exactly this reason. The screens are built - they just need honouring

What to do: Give a person a ring time before voicemail
Why it matters: There is no setting anywhere for how long a phone rings. Queues have one per member; a person does not. Customers change this in week one
Notes: Dialpad uses 30 seconds, Genesys 12 with a 60 max. Pick 30 and allow 5-60

What to do: A company endpoint a customer admin can actually use
Why it matters: A customer cannot correct their own company name or registered address. The only endpoint is restricted to platform staff
Notes: Should read the company from the sign-in token, not from the request body. The screen is already built and waiting

What to do: Make a location set the clock for people there
Why it matters: A location currently decides nothing. Opening hours read each person's own timezone, so a London queue can run on Mumbai time
Notes: Our own screen already tells customers a location sets the clock. It does not

What to do: An emergency address on each location
Why it matters: A company with two offices has one emergency address. Anyone at the second office sends the wrong address
Notes: Do this together with item 3

What to do: Let admins choose which location is the main one
Why it matters: It is marked in the list but cannot be changed. Genesys warns that inbound calls fail when this is wrong
Notes: Small change, prevents a confusing failure

What to do: Make retention actually delete things
Why it matters: The settings save but no job deletes anything. Customers cannot answer a compliance question with it
Notes: Genesys's model is the better one: keep / archive / delete with a day count

What to do: Controls for who can hear recordings
Why it matters: No way to say whether people hear their own recordings, or whether admins hear everyone's. This is a privacy question customers ask early
Notes: Dialpad emails every non-admin when the admin-access setting changes. Worth copying

What to do: Voicemail email controls: send at all, personal details, transcript
Why it matters: Three separate GDPR-relevant switches we do not have at all
Notes: Genesys forces personal details off for healthcare accounts

What to do: Split company admins from location admins
Why it matters: One rule prevents most privilege problems: only a company admin may create another admin or change retention
Notes: Needs item 2 done first

What to do: Apply one holiday to many lines at once
Why it matters: We built the holiday list but it has to be applied to each queue, menu and person one at a time
Notes: Cheapest win on this sheet - the import logic already exists

What to do: Finish the voicemail PIN screen
Why it matters: The value is stored and shown on the summary card, but the editor is commented out - nobody can set it
Notes: Half-built already. Either finish it or remove the display

What to do: Raise the 10-holiday limit on a line
Why it matters: The US federal list is 11 holidays, so a full US year does not fit
Notes: Small. Raise to 25

What to do: Enforce two-step sign-in
Why it matters: Screen is built and saves; nothing enforces it
Notes: Dialpad makes it mandatory for anyone not on single sign-on. Copy that posture

What to do: Enforce idle sign-out
Why it matters: Screen is built and saves; nothing signs anyone out
Notes: Genesys allows 5 minutes to 8 hours

What to do: Single sign-on (SAML)
Why it matters: We record the details but no sign-on uses them. Needed for larger customers
Notes: Blocks enterprise deals, not small ones

What to do: Restrict sign-in by network
Why it matters: Stored and validated; nothing restricts anything
Notes: Genesys allows up to 150 ranges

What to do: Being open part of a holiday
Why it matters: A holiday is all-day only today

What to do: Default country code for buying numbers
Why it matters: Small quality-of-life item when adding numbers

What to do: Spam call blocking
Why it matters: Dialpad blocks automatically and offers per-person screening
Notes: Depends on a spam-score source

What to do: Let a phone menu forward to an outside number
Why it matters: A company master switch, off by default
Notes: Dialpad restricts this to domestic numbers for good reason

What to do: AI training opt in or out
Why it matters: We have heavy AI features and no way for a customer to opt out. GDPR relevant
Notes: Dialpad defaults: US and Canada opt out, UK and EU opt in

What to do: Password rules
Why it matters: Length, characters, expiry
Notes: Enterprise RFP material. Not needed until asked

What to do: Reusable schedules shared across queues
Why it matters: Genesys's real advantage: one schedule used by hundreds of queues
Notes: Only worth it once customers run many queues. Do NOT half-do this

What to do: Several offices under one account
Why it matters: Large architecture change. Locations already cover most of the need
Notes: Revisit only if customers ask for separate billing per office

What to do: Caller ID name (CNAM)
Why it matters: Carrier-dependent, US and Canada only, 7-10 days to take effect
Notes: Slow and outside our control however well we build it

What to do: Local area code when calling out
Why it matters: US only, paid add-on, carrier-dependent

What to do: Emergency address that follows a travelling user
Why it matters: US and Canada, desktop app only
Notes: Do the basic emergency address first (item 3)

What to do: Cost centres for reporting
Why it matters: Tags for reporting only - changes no invoice or total
Notes: Pure reporting. No customer is blocked by this

What to do: Bring your own encryption key
Why it matters: Enterprise checkbox item
Notes: Build when an RFP demands it, not before

What to do: One-off purge of existing data
Why it matters: Cannot be undone. Dangerous before retention itself works
Notes: Build after item 10, never before

What to do: Support access pairing link
Why it matters: This is for a vendor getting into a customer account - you ARE the vendor
Notes: Not applicable to your position

What to do: Copy settings from another office / bulk office switches
Why it matters: Both need several offices to exist first
Notes: Depends on item 28

What to do: Automated 'delete my data' request pipeline
Why it matters: Handle these by hand until the volume justifies a system
